scenario: An archaeology field school admits students if they have either elite surveying skill or elite epigraphy skill. A 10% wildcard also admits students with neither trait. Faculty think the two skills are negatively related among admitted students.

data.description: Admission is based on either trait plus a wildcard.

question: Among admitted students, compute (a) P(surveying | epigraphy, selected), and (b) P(surveying | not epigraphy, selected). Is the negative association real or a selection artifact?

ground_truth.explanation: The apparent negative association arises from conditioning on admission.

naive_answer: Surveying and epigraphy seem to trade off among admitted students.
naive_trap: Admission on either skill creates collider bias.
